# Course planning contract

Placement computation remains independent of planning. Explicit diagnostic
INITIAL planning uses the plan ID as its stable key. Recovery reads the exact
plan-bound request and resumes only terminal exhaustion. An immutable allocation
checkpoint precedes Student assignment/allocation; replay has priority over
mutable graph/profile/mastery reads and retains the original desired body.
Before that checkpoint, normal diagnostic context validation stays in force.
New-path NO_GAP remains terminal without creating a LearningPath.

## Identity

Learning targets use exact `(type, key, version)` identity. Supported types are `concept` and `capability`. Planner never derives targets from titles or generated text.

Learning Planner is the canonical target catalog. Design-time consumers such as
TZ Planner resolve proposed blueprint targets through
`POST /internal/learning-targets/resolve`; any item in `missing` makes the
authoring candidate ineligible for publication.

Before generation, TZ Planner obtains a bounded vocabulary through
`POST /internal/learning-targets/candidates`. Optional stack filters use
`learning_target_stack`; no filter returns at most 200 definitions. Discovery
never substitutes for exact resolution and never creates aliases.

## Ownership and Course lifecycle

Planner owns the reviewed target/prerequisite graph and Course design/generation workflow; it is the architectural replacement for a separate Knowledge Tree service in the current scope. Teacher supplies a goal, desired outcome, requested exact skills, bounded preferences, and audit references. Teacher does not calculate gaps or generate Course content.

Planner requests Course to atomically reuse or create a private `ACTIVE` Course. The hierarchy remains `Course -> Module -> Section -> Lesson -> Task`; generated Lessons are `ACTIVE` only after all typed content succeeds. Course owns canonical rows, status enums, task contracts, access rules, and later content lifecycle.

## Graph readiness v1

The default-off `PLANNER_GRAPH_READINESS_ENABLED` gate protects a separate
read-only Teacher query. While it is off, Planner fails before any Student or
database call. When enabled, Planner reads the strict Student-owned
`student-planning-readiness-snapshot.v1`; the caller cannot supply or override
profile, goal, graph, stack, language, active-path, or mastery facts.

Resolver `learning-readiness-resolver-v1` has two exact positive rules:

- `learn_programming`, `beginner`, direction `undecided`, desired stacks either
  `unanswered` or explicitly `answered` with `[]`, and a trusted Student
  `content_language` select `programming.foundation`;
- `learn_programming`, direction `backend`, exactly desired stack `[go]`, a
  present valid self-assessed experience, and trusted `content_language`
  select the existing `go.backend` goal.

Student currently emits `unanswered` for the normal no-selection flow.
Planner accepts answered-empty only as a strict defensive DTO state; Student
does not manufacture it and S6 does not loosen the existing write contract.

Known stacks never select a graph. Optional weekly minutes and pace never
change the decision. Multiple, unresolved, or contradictory combinations need
clarification; other complete combinations are not ready. There are no aliases,
fuzzy matches, first-published choices, or fallback goals.

Planner then loads only the exact `PUBLISHED` goal and validates its complete
placement, transition, and prerequisite topology. External prerequisites,
self-edges, cycles, and conflicting placements fail closed. `READY` means only
that a published graph resolved: it is explicitly non-executable and no
content exists yet. It does not create or predict a Course, Learning Path, or
Lesson identity. A Student-owned active path always takes precedence and is
returned only as an unchanged observational reference.

## Durable onboarding plan handoff v1

S8 adds a separately feature-gated immutable Planner receipt for a Teacher
dialog that has already reached exact S6 graph readiness. It is not a
`course_plan_request`: acceptance records only bounded Student state, dialog,
and Teacher-job UUIDs plus the exact published goal identity. It does not invoke
Course, AI Prompt, Student writes, path/lesson creation, worker, outbox, or
NATS.

`PLANNER_ONBOARDING_HANDOFF_ENABLED` defaults false and can only be enabled
with `PLANNER_GRAPH_READINESS_ENABLED=true`. A disabled endpoint can return an
exact previously stored idempotent receipt without reading Student; it rejects
an unseen key before any Student or graph call. New acceptance re-reads the
authoritative Student snapshot, binds the request `expected_state_ref`, then
accepts only `READY`, `executable=false`, and `content_status=NOT_CREATED`.
The unique `(student_id, state_ref_kind, state_ref_version)` fence prevents a
second handoff for the same Student-owned snapshot even under different keys.
`readiness_observed_at` records the canonical UTC instant when Planner received
that authoritative result; `created_at` is never earlier. This is a historical
admission only, not a no-active-path reservation. A path that appears after
that observation does not rewrite the immutable receipt; S9 must independently
re-read and atomically reserve Student state before any executable effect.

## S9 onboarding path execution

S9 is a separately flagged durable executor, not a `course_plan_request`.
It re-reads strict Student readiness and obtains a Student-owned atomic
admission before AI Prompt or Course effects. Its frozen
`planner-onboarding-path-authoring-input.v1` carries exact graph topology/hash,
policy identity, trusted content language, and only Student fields that are
present; missing preferences remain absent. Lesson enrichment stays behind the
confidential `course.lesson-content.v1` boundary and the complete parsed Course
draft is persisted before Course ensure. Student reserve, renewal, materialize,
and abort each use a different deterministic UUID-v5 idempotency key; a renewal
key is bound to its current persisted fence. The admission receipt/fence/expiry
is checkpointed before content work, so a crash replays the exact Student
operation instead of attempting a new reservation. Only `PATH_READY`,
`ACTIVE_PATH_EXISTS`, and `STATE_CHANGED` commit a bounded S9 outcome outbox
event. Internal `FAILED` evidence remains durable but intentionally emits no
public S9 outcome.

Each ordered lesson uses only `course.lesson-content.v1` with the frozen S9
course context and lesson plan. The parsed result, SHA-256, and deterministic
AI idempotency identity are durable before moving to the next lesson. Retries
reuse those rows and never call a completed lesson prompt again.

## Objective skip rule

Policy `course-planner-v1` skips a target only when Student returns `MASTERED` with confidence at least `0.80`. Declared stacks and self-assessment may select transition explanations but never skip a target.

## CourseFingerprint v1

Canonical input contains goal and graph versions, normalized relevant onboarding dimensions, sorted relevant stacks, ordered exact target decisions (`INCLUDE` or `SKIP`), ordered gap targets, applicable reviewed transition knowledge, planner version, pedagogy profile version, presentation style version, and generation policy version. Exact scores are normalized to the decision actually affecting Course structure, avoiding one Course per insignificant score variation.

Student ID, timestamps, raw evidence, request identity, source/reason, free-text desired outcome, deadline, project context, and dialog/decision audit references are excluded. They therefore cannot leak into a shared Course or churn an unchanged replan. Requested targets affect the graph closure and gap set rather than appearing as duplicate fingerprint metadata. The SHA-256 lower-hex digest is stored with `fingerprint_version=course-fingerprint-v1`.

## Private planning checkpoints

Before content generation or any Course/Student write, the active worker pins
its first assembled input through the separate `PinnedCoursePlanRepository`
port on the request repository. The private versioned record binds request,
Student, request hash, goal and intent to normalized profile, objective mastery,
graph, policy, diagnostic route and original onboarding/direction fences,
original exact path snapshot or nil, deterministic draft, fingerprint, normalized
context bytes and gap targets. This is bounded historical job provenance;
Student remains the owner of current learner state. The SHA-256 input hash is a
private job identity and does not change `course-fingerprint-v1` or its exclusions.

The complete typed generated Course is immutably checkpointed against that input
hash before Course ensure. The actual ensure receipt, including ordered exact
lesson and revision bindings, is checkpointed against both hashes before Student
assignment or path effects. A reconstructed worker uses these original records;
it does not reread current profile, mastery, graph or policy to replace their
fingerprint or generation keys. Partial generation can replay the same
request/fingerprint/placement keys against the original input. Checkpoint write
ambiguity stops effects and is recovered by reading the durable record on the
next claim. Hash, identity or typed checkpoint validation failures stop the job.

Existing exact-path command and diagnostic initial-allocation checkpoints replay
first, preserving legacy exact-body retry behavior. If a new private input is
present, replay validates it and restores its original fingerprint/context audit
bytes before dispatch; absent pins preserve legacy command replay. A legacy active request with
`generated_course_json` but no trustworthy planning-input checkpoint terminates
with `LEGACY_GENERATED_COURSE_UNBOUND`; it is never guessed or backfilled. Completed
jobs remain historical. Original exact-path expected versions and diagnostic
onboarding/direction fences still reach Student unchanged, and delivered stale
application conflicts retain their existing terminal behavior. This change adds
no global mastery revision fence, generic INITIAL admission rule, or new quality,
stability, consent, or skip policy. Those application limits remain separate work.

## Typed generation

Every planned lesson receives a UUID-v5 idempotency key derived from planning request, fingerprint, and ordered placement. AI Prompt returns exactly `description_markdown`, 1–12 examples, and 1–12 knowledge checks under `course.lesson-content.v1`; unknown fields, oversized values, and untyped responses fail closed. Targets, prerequisites, placement, pedagogy strategies, and runtime validation contracts never come from the model. Course creates fixed Course-owned `quiz_theory` contracts and copies authoritative lesson targets to each generated task.

## Path targeting, replan, and delivery

The following describes the current executable contract. Evidence/Mastery-driven
adaptation is governed by the accepted [Hybrid Replanning decision](hybrid-mastery-replanning.md):
evaluation is separate from mutation, Planner returns a desired mutation, and
Student applies it at a safe boundary with snapshot freshness and protected-state
checks. This architectural decision adds no fields or endpoints to this contract
and does not establish that the full target flow is implemented.

`INITIAL` forbids a caller-supplied path. After Course ensure and the separate
Course assignment command, Student allocates exactly one path using the
planning request UUID as both planning and idempotency identity. Planner
checkpoints the returned path ID before later side effects. For newly pinned jobs, a crash retry replays the original create body with
that same request key and checks the returned path against the resolved ID.
The original nil path remains nil in the planning input; a later resolved ID
never turns that initial decision into a replan. An older ungenerated job with
an already resolved exact path may retain its existing reconciliation behavior;
its first pin records that exact path snapshot without inventing caller input.

A `REPLAN` requires `learning_path_id`, includes it in the request hash, and
reads planning state by exact `(student_id,path_id)`. The selected/primary path
from the learner overview is never substituted. Planner sends desired Course
identity/fingerprint plus ordered `READY`/`PLANNED` references. Student owns
monotonic progress reconciliation, frozen targets for progressed matching
references, and path/journey version increments. An unchanged effective route
is a Student semantic no-op. Course assignment remains a separate idempotent
command rather than being hidden inside path reconciliation.

Immediately before either exact-path `REPLAN` or `NO_GAP`, Planner commits an
immutable checkpoint on the claimed request. It contains the normalized exact
body, expected Student path version, command kind, timestamp, and SHA-256 that
also binds Student, path, planning request, and the identical Student
`Idempotency-Key`. The private planned terminal outcome required to finish the
job is bound by the same hash and checkpointed in the same update. Public
`result_code`, `course_id`, and `reused` stay unset until Student success is
confirmed. If the success response is lost, the next
claim dispatches that checkpoint directly: it does not reload the path, graph,
mastery, Course result, or construct a new expected version/body. Student's
receipt therefore returns the original result. A delivered Student `409` is a
known concurrent conflict and terminates the request with
`LEARNING_PATH_COMMAND_CONFLICT`; retry is reserved for ambiguous transport or
transient availability failures.

Terminal completion/failure commits with a schema-v2 outbox envelope carrying
the optional exact path ID. Teacher consumes only Teacher-originated outcomes
with dialog audit references and reports the business result idempotently; no
chain-of-thought or generation trace is published.
The retained checkpoint body/hash/planned outcome are private operational audit
fields and are not copied into HTTP responses or events. Only after confirmed
Student success is the planned outcome copied into the terminal completed row.

## No-gap result

If every required target is objectively mastered, the planning request
completes with `result_code=NO_GAP`, no Course is created, and `course_id` is
absent. For `REPLAN` or a checkpointed `INITIAL`, Planner asks Student to
idempotently mark remaining items `SKIPPED_MASTERED` on only that exact
same-goal path. A new unallocated `INITIAL` creates no path, and
selected/primary paths with other IDs are never changed.

The complete generated Course JSON document is limited to 16 MiB. This total
bound complements the per-field and per-lesson limits and is enforced before
the Course command.

## Practice route v1

`practice-learning-route-request.v1` is competency-first. Each ordered Step
contains stable requirement IDs, exact target refs, one of `required`,
`recommended`, `optional`, or `adaptive`, and an explicit mastery threshold.
It never contains lesson UUIDs.

Only `MASTERED` evidence whose mastery score meets the requirement threshold
and whose confidence meets the active Planner policy is satisfied. Required
gaps return blocking `LEARN`; recommended and optional gaps remain
non-blocking; adaptive gaps return blocking `CHALLENGE_OR_LEARN` with an
assessment option. The returned `student-task-learning-snapshot.v1` includes
deterministic material identities but no generated lesson content.

The task instance UUID is the idempotency key. Planner persists one immutable
resolution receipt so retries do not reinterpret changed mastery or policy.
Practice is the canonical owner of the frozen snapshot used by runtime.

## Lazy practice material v1

Every unresolved route item identifies reusable content by the SHA-256 of its
exact target, locale, planner/pedagogy/presentation/generation policies, and
selected pedagogy strategy versions. `ensure` first proves that identity is
present in the immutable route. It then invokes `course.lesson-content.v1`
with a deterministic generation UUID and sends a complete single-Lesson
private Course to Course under `practice-material-fingerprint-v1`. Retries use
the same AI and Course idempotency identities; compatible task instances reuse
the same Course-owned material.

## Diagnostic assessment plan v1

`POST /api/learning-planner/v1/diagnostic-assessment-plans` is the
actor-scoped `diagnostic-assessment-bootstrap.v1` contract. Its strict body
contains only the Student onboarding version and an optional explicit retake
revision; it never accepts a Course, goal, direction, stack, score, band, or
task identity. Planner reads authoritative Student onboarding, resolves the
latest exact rollout-provisioned `(goal_code,direction_code)` binding (no
fallback), then reads Course's exact `course-diagnostic-assessment-catalog.v1`
and deterministically freezes three to five content-spread `AUTO` assessments
under `diagnostic-fixed-v1`. A successful issue response is conditional on a
durable replay-safe Student reservation receipt keyed by the plan ID; Planner
stores only that safe delivery proof, never attempt state.

Retakes use the same bootstrap route with `expected_previous_revision`. It must
equal the latest revision for the same immutable bootstrap context, which must already have an immutable placement
decision; revision increments once and receives a distinct deterministic plan
and attempt ID. Revision 1 is deterministic within its bootstrap context; the
pre-bootstrap formula was never deployed. A reused
issuance key replays its exact revision; a changed request hash conflicts.

Teacher's private `POST` and `GET`
`/internal/students/{studentID}/diagnostic-assessment-plans/{planID}/placement`
consume only Student's completed aggregate result. The sole route mapping is
`FOUNDATION -> START_FOUNDATION`, `CORE -> START_CORE`, and `ADVANCED ->
START_ADVANCED` under `diagnostic-placement-route-v1`. The stored
`diagnostic-placement.v1` decision contains bindings, aggregate, policies,
digests, timestamps, and route only—never questions, answers, task IDs,
correctness by item, scorer state, mastery, paths, progress, or evidence. No
diagnostic action mutates Student state or calls Course/Practice after issuance.
The shared fixed plan includes `onboarding_version`, exact
`bootstrap_policy_version=diagnostic-bootstrap-v1`, and
`bootstrap_context_digest`; binding identity stays in Planner's internal
receipt and is never sent to Student as part of the strict plan DTO.

## Project authoring flow

Planner owns `PROPOSED -> CONFIRMED -> AUTHORING -> READY -> PUBLISHED` for a
project recommendation bound to one exact current Student Learning Path
snapshot. Its immutable input contains only path/goal identity and bounded
target, locale, and stack references needed for a PII-free TZ v2 request.
The flow also freezes the authoritative onboarding version and a deterministic
`planner-project-authoring-profile.v1` digest over the profile contract version,
derived locale, and ordered deduplicated TZ-canonical desired stack codes. Each
stack code is capped at 64 bytes. The worker recomputes both profile provenance
and the path digest before authoring, accepting READY, and publishing.
Answers, profile/mastery snapshots, generated source, and private verification
data are forbidden.

Teacher confirmation is explicit and idempotent. The worker revalidates the
same owner provenance before authoring and before accepting READY. TZ owns the job
and verified artifact. READY is not publication: another Teacher command must
persist an explicit publication request before Planner calls TZ publish.
PUBLISHED stores the immutable Practice revision receipt but cannot start
Practice, create Sandbox state, mutate Student progress, or complete a path
item.

For locator loss, Teacher can request the current flow by exact Student/path.
Planner reloads the selected ACTIVE owner state, derives the same path and
authoring-profile provenance, and returns only a non-FAILED exact match. Thus a
changed path or profile returns no stale flow. Different create idempotency keys
for the same immutable snapshot converge on its original live flow; the
original key and flow identity are never rewritten. `FAILED` permits a new flow
for the snapshot, while `PUBLISHED` remains recoverable for it.

## Lesson completion assignment cutover

Course ensure returns an exact immutable `lesson_revision_id` for every lesson
binding. Planner forwards it unchanged into new allocation, exact-path replan,
and onboarding materialization commands. Student resolves that revision and
freezes completion requirements; Planner never supplies or interprets them.

Planning-state items expose optional `learning_path_item_id` and
`lesson_revision_id`. Replan retains an existing item ID only for the same
lesson and exact revision, matching repeated occurrences in order. Unmatched
revision references omit the item ID so Student assigns a new identity. Desired
routes may repeat the same revision, while returned owner states must carry
distinct item IDs. Legacy references without revisions keep their established
semantics and are never given a fabricated historical revision. Existing
checkpoint bodies replay unchanged; they are not upgraded on retry.

## Automatic diagnostic placement

Student's official completion transaction emits `student.diagnostic-result.committed.v1`
(schema 1) through its durable outbox. Planner consumes it independently of the
browser using the existing protected Student result GET capability and the
unchanged `diagnostic-placement-route-v1` policy. This automatically persists only
an immutable placement receipt. Course planning, initial path allocation, mastery,
progress, and runtime actions still require their separate authorized commands.

The existing event envelope contains `event_id`, `event_type`, `correlation_id`,
`causation_id`, `student_id`, `occurred_at`, `schema_version`, and exactly the data
fields `plan_id`, `plan_revision`, `plan_digest`, `result_digest`. The event UUID is
SHA1 in the URL namespace over subject + `:` + plan ID. Correlation is the plan
and attempt ID, causation is the completion request UUID, and occurrence time is
the canonical UTC microsecond completion timestamp. No score, band, answers,
mastery, or profile is transmitted. Planner rejects unknown or duplicate JSON
fields, null/missing fields, oversized bodies/headers, subject/schema mismatches,
and missing/duplicate/mismatched event, correlation, causation, or schema headers.

Before any placement write, Planner verifies its own frozen plan identity,
revision, student, and digest, then reads Student's authoritative aggregate and
verifies its result digest and completion timestamp against the event. Replay
first validates the existing immutable receipt and all event references, so a
valid delivery can finish during a Student outage without recalculating a route.
The browser/Teacher placement endpoint remains compatible recovery.

Startup uses the existing `NATS_URL`, without a feature flag, and requires the
infrastructure-owned `STUDENT_DIAGNOSTIC_EVENTS` file workqueue stream for only
this subject: no age/message expiry, 1 GiB capacity, discard new, ten-minute
publication deduplication, one replica. Missing or incompatible streams fail
startup. The subscriber never creates, resets, or updates the stream. It creates
or binds only `ms-learning-planner-diagnostic-placement-v1`, deliver all, explicit
ACK, unlimited delivery attempts, 30-second ACK wait, one pending ACK. ACK follows
the committed receipt; invalid events terminate without placement, while transient
owner/storage failures receive NAK with a two-second retry delay. Shutdown cancels
and waits for the owned consumer loop, unsubscribes without deleting the durable,
and closes its connection. Unacknowledged messages survive service restart.

Historical completed attempts that predate the new transactional event are not
automatically backfilled. Their existing explicit placement recovery remains
available; this rollout introduces no migration or historical result rewrite.
